chapter: Cab Calloway on the road and segregation
title: Cab Calloway's band as the high point, and first-class travel
summary: Cheatham calls Cab the high point of his career, with Pullman travel unlike the raggedy buses of the Cotton Pickers and Alabamians.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I want to -- in our next session I want to get into -- go from say mid-'40's up to the present time. But, just before we stop this, let me just see if there's anything else we have left out. What would you say up to 1946, what -- what was the high light -- the high point of your career, was it Cab Calloway band, was it the Cotton Pickers?
It was the Cab Calloway band.
Cab's a very important part of my life.
Now that was a lot of travelling, it was very popular band --
Lot of travelling, but first class.
Uh-huh, but you didn't mind the touring?
I didn't mind it because it was all first class. We had no -- it wasn't like the Cotton Pickers, or the Alabamians where you were riding buses, a -- old raggedy buses, break down every few miles.
Sleeping in the buses, eating cold cuts, being run out of places, being run out of town and all this stuff. With Cab it was first class all the way. Slept on Pullmans' side track to sleep.
